title: No Time to Lift? Designing Time-Efficient Training Programs for Strength and Hypertrophy: A Narrative Review

citation: Zhang et al. Sports Medicine (2025). DOI: 10.1007/s40279-025-02176-8.
title: Superset Versus Traditional Resistance Training Prescriptions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Exploring Acute and Chronic Effects on Mechanical, Metabolic, and Perceptual Variables

population.description: Predominantly young, trained men; 19 studies, only three chronic

intervention: Supersets of different configurations; protocols varied
results: Shorter sessions and higher perceived effort; limited chronic evidence suggests broadly similar adaptations, not proven equivalence.
harms: Adverse-event data not extracted; safety cannot be concluded

reasons: Concealment/blinding information missing; small chronic evidence base; heterogeneity

funding_conflicts: Open-access funding: Universidad de Granada/CBUA; no commercial/financial conflicts declared. Other funding not extracted.
notes: Selected methods/results/limitations reviewed; formal independent appraisal incomplete.

citation: Haugen et al. BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation (2023).
title: Effect of free-weight vs. machine-based strength training on maximal strength, hypertrophy and jump performance

population.description: Healthy adults; 13 studies; outcome populations differ

intervention: Free-weight training for at least six weeks
results: Testing specificity matters; hypertrophy comparisons did not detect a difference.

reasons: Sparse outcome-specific evidence; independent study-level appraisal incomplete

directness: Does not evaluate every substitute or crowded-gym scenario
notes: Selected methods/results reviewed. Review search ended January 1, 2023; update incomplete.

title: Less time, same gains: Comparison of superset vs traditional set training on muscular adaptations
study_design: randomized controlled training trial, preprint record

population.description: Young resistance-trained men and women, as reported in abstract

intervention: Supervised supersets twice weekly for eight weeks
results: Author abstract reports shorter sessions and similar average adaptation estimates.

reasons: Abstract-only appraisal; final journal record not verified

directness: Supervised protocol, not proof for all pairings
notes: Same cohort as later journal lead; deduplicate, do not treat as replication.
